title: Private Deployments: VPC & On-Prem Reference Architectures, Packaging, Day-2 Ops, Upgrades & Rollbacks, Customer Requirements Library
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Summary
This document consolidates the canonical guidance for Redwood Private deployments (VPC and on-prem packaged deployments). It covers reference architectures, recommended on-prem packaging and installation patterns, day-2 operational processes, and our standardized upgrade and rollback procedures. A customer requirements library is included to accelerate presales, security reviews, and implementation planning.

Scope and audience
- Scope: End-to-end deployment lifecycle for Redwood Private (VPC and on-prem). Includes pre-sales requirements, deployment architecture, packaging options, installation checklist, day-2 runbooks, upgrade/rollback runbooks, and ownership model.
- Audience: Solutions engineers, deployment engineers, SREs, customer infra teams, and product/security reviewers.

High-level goals
- Provide repeatable reference architectures for common customer topologies (single-cluster, multi-cluster HA, air-gapped on-prem).
- Standardize packaging artifacts and installation commands to reduce onboarding time.
- Define day-2 operational procedures (monitoring, backups, scale, incident handling).
- Produce deterministic upgrade and rollback steps with safety gates and automated checks.
- Maintain a customer requirements library to streamline scoping and security questionnaires.

Reference architectures (textual diagrams)
1) VPC-hosted Private control plane + customer data plane (recommended for most enterprise customers)
   - Components: Redwood control plane (managed by Redwood, private tenancy), Customer VPC containing data plane (Kubernetes cluster(s) or bare-metal), VPN or AWS PrivateLink/Transit Gateway for control-plane connectivity.
   - Traffic flow: Control plane <-> Data plane for: model pulls, metrics, config sync. Customer traffic stays inside customer VPC.
   - High-level benefits: minimal on-site footprint, faster updates, stronger auditability.

2) Fully on-prem (air-gapped) deployment
   - Components: Local control plane (customer-managed), on-prem inference cluster (GPU nodes), on-prem registry & artifact repository, internal key management (HSM/KMS).
   - Data flow: No outbound internet; model artifacts transferred via secure air-gap procedures or pre-seeded local registry.
   - High-level benefits: meets highest compliance/regulatory needs.

3) Hybrid multi-region HA (large customers)
   - Components: Redundant data plane clusters in multiple regions, global load balancer, regional cache nodes for KV/prefix caching, failover policies.
   - SLO target: 99.95% availability across regions with cross-region fallback.

Minimum hardware and capacity guidance (table described)
- Minimum single-node inference (dev/test): 1x 8GB GPU (e.g., T4), 32GB RAM, 2 vCPU equivalent, 100GB local disk.
- Production baseline (small): 4x 16GB GPUs (A10/T4 equivalent), 256GB RAM, 16 vCPU, 1TB NVMe for model cache.
- Production HA (recommended): 3 availability zones, each with 4+ inference GPUs, dedicated autoscaling group for workers, separate control-plane instances.
- On-prem high-throughput: Balanced GPU types depending on model family (A100/RTX6000), local NVMe cache for model shards, 100Gbps networking between GPU hosts for large-scale KV sync.

Network & security requirements (ports and policies)
- Control plane connectivity: outbound TLS (443) to Redwood control endpoints OR private connectivity via AWS PrivateLink/Transit Gateway.
- Required ports (example table):
  - 443/tcp: control plane API (TLS)
  - 50051/tcp: gRPC internal (if enabled)
  - 22/tcp: ops access (restricted)
  - 9100-9200/tcp: node exporters/metrics (restricted to monitoring subnet)
- Firewall and Egress: For restricted customers we offer an egress-minimal mode where only model pulls and health-checks are allowed over a dedicated peering connection.

On-prem packaging and installation patterns
- Packaging artifacts: Helm charts for Kubernetes, systemd unit tarball for bare-metal, immutable appliance image (OVA) for VMware. All artifacts are signed and accompanied by a SHA256 manifest.
- Installation options:
  1) Helm install (Kubernetes) - recommended for cloud and customer-managed K8s:
     - Pre-requisites: Kubernetes 1.22+, Helm 3.7+, PV support for model cache.
     - Example (high-level):
       - wget https://artifacts.redwood.ai/package/redwood-private-2027.1.tgz
       - helm repo add redwood https://charts.redwood.ai/stable
       - helm install redwood-private redwood/redwood --namespace redwood --values values-production.yaml
  2) On-prem appliance (VMware/OVA) - recommended for regulated customers with restricted admin teams.
  3) Bare-metal systemd-based installer - for dedicated GPU hosts where Kubernetes is not desired.
- Packaging notes: All releases are published with release notes, compatibility matrix, and a "packaging manifest" that lists supported OS, driver versions, and required kernel modules (e.g., nvidia driver >= 525, CUDA 12.x compatibility).

Pre-deployment checklist (numbered)
1) Validate customer network reachability and DNS records for control-plane endpoints.
2) Confirm GPU driver and CUDA versions on target hosts.
3) Confirm KMS/HSM availability and key provisioning.
4) Verify storage performance (IOPS, latency) for model cache.
5) Run the preflight diagnostics bundle provided with the release and capture outputs.

Day-2 operations (runbook highlights)
- Monitoring and observability
  - Required metrics: per-route latency (p50/p95/p99), tokens/sec, model cache hit rate, KV cache saturation, GPU utilization by device.
  - Dashboards: Pre-built Grafana dashboards shipped with Helm chart. Ensure metrics retention policy is set per customer SLAs.
  - Alerts (examples):
    - latency.p95 > 500ms for >5min -> P1 alert to SRE/Customer Support.
    - model-cache-miss-rate > 30% sustained -> P2, recommend scale event.
- Backup & restore
  - Backups: periodic snapshots of configuration (control-plane DB), model registry metadata, and critical logs. For on-prem air-gapped installs, backups are exported to secure SAN and encrypted with customer KMS.
  - Restore test cadence: quarterly restore drills recommended.
- Scaling and capacity management
  - Autoscaling rules: Use GPU utilization > 75% averaged over 3 minutes as a scale-up trigger. Cooldown: 10 minutes.
  - Cache warmup: After scale-up, run model-prefetch jobs to warm local NVMe cache to reduce cold-start latency.
- Incident response
  - Typical incidents: model corruption, disk pressure on cache nodes, GPU driver faults, control-plane sync failures.
  - Initial triage checklist: check node health, check model registry integrity (sha256), review recent control-plane sync logs, apply fallback model variant if necessary.

Upgrade procedure (safe, staged)
- Strategy: Canary -> Regional -> Global with automated health gates. Always run upgrades against a non-production canary namespace prior to production rollout.
- High-level steps (numbered):
  1) Read release notes and compatibility/driver matrix.
  2) Run the upgrade preflight script: ./tools/preflight-check.sh --release redwood-private-2027.1
  3) Snapshot control-plane DB and export model registry metadata.
  4) Apply upgrade in canary namespace: helm upgrade --namespace redwood-canary redwood redwood/redwood --version 2027.1 -f canary-values.yaml
  5) Run integration smoke tests (latency, generation correctness, KV-cache behavior).
  6) Observe health gates for a minimum of 30 minutes: no P1/P2 alerts, p95 latency not increased by >15%, model output regression <1% on golden prompt set.
  7) If gates pass, progressively rollout to additional namespaces/regions.
  8) Post-upgrade regression evaluation: run full eval harness to detect quality regressions and notify Applied ML team.

Rollback procedure (fast, deterministic)
- Rollback triggers: failed canary health gates, production P1 alert with suspected regression, or data-plane desynchronization that blocks traffic.
- Rollback steps (numbered):
  1) Stop rollouts and isolate impacted namespaces.
  2) Restore control-plane from snapshot (if control-plane DB schema changed and cannot be forward-compat).
  3) helm rollback <release> <revision> --namespace <ns> OR re-deploy previous chart version: helm upgrade --version <previous> -f previous-values.yaml
  4) If model artifacts were changed and corruption is suspected, verify model registry checksums and re-pull artifacts from signed blob store.
  5) Run smoke tests and confirm health gates before re-opening public endpoints.
  6) Post-incident: file RCA and register a regression ticket with Applied ML and Release Engineering.

Automated safety gates and metrics for upgrades
- Mandatory gates: p95 latency delta <= +15% vs baseline, error-rate delta <= +0.5%, cache hit-rate not degraded by more than 10%.
- Quality gates: run golden prompt set through canary for semantic regression detection (automated script returns pass/fail).

Customer requirements library (scoped checklist and templates)
- Security & compliance template (shortlist):
  - Network: support for PrivateLink / Transit Gateway / VPN, list of required ports.
  - Data: models do not leave customer VPC; optional telemetry with opt-in.
  - KMS: support for external HSM or cloud KMS with BYOK.
  - Audit: admin activity logs, model pull audit trail retained for configurable retention up to 7 years.
- Operational readiness template (shortlist):
  - Admins: list of customer admin principals and IAM roles.
  - Monitoring: metrics ingestion endpoint and Grafana access controls.
  - Capacity: expected QPS, model size, concurrency targets, and estimated GPU count.
- Legal / contractual checklist (shortlist):
  - Data residency constraints, breach notification SLA, and support response times.

Preflight diagnostic bundle (how to run)
- Command (Kubernetes examples):
  - curl -sSfL https://artifacts.redwood.ai/preflight/preflight-2027.1.sh | bash -s -- --kubeconfig /path/to/kubeconfig --target-nodes node1,node2
- Output: JSON manifest with node capabilities, driver versions, network path checks, and recommended remediation actions. Attach this manifest to the deployment ticket.

Ownership, escalation and contacts
- Deployment owner: eng-private-deployments team (primary: Aisha Patel).
- On-call escalation: private-deployments SRE rotation -> applied-ml -> product -> security (for data incidents).
- Slack channels: #private-deployments, #sec-incident (restricted).
- Pager duty: eng-private-deployments-oncall.

Operational checklists (quick)
- Daily: check health dashboard, confirm no alert > 5 minutes, verify control-plane sync status.
- Weekly: run backup verification, review model registry integrity checks, rotate ephemeral credentials.
- Monthly: capacity planning review, run canary upgrade in staging.

Appendices
- Appendix A: Compatibility matrix (examples)
  - Redwood private 2027.1 -> nvidia driver >=525, CUDA 12.x, Kubernetes >=1.22
- Appendix B: Example values-production.yaml highlights (Kubernetes)
  - replicaCounts: gateway:3, workers:6
  - resources: worker.gpuRequests: 1
  - cache: localNvmeSizeGb: 1024
- Appendix C: Example rollback playbook snippet (one-liner)
  - helm rollback redwood-private 12 --namespace redwood ; kubectl rollout status deploy/redwood-worker -n redwood

Document maintenance
- Owners: eng-private-deployments (primary), applied-ml (quality gates), eng-sre (runbooks/alerts).
- Review cadence: Quarterly review or after every major release.
- Related artifacts: release notes, packaging manifests, preflight tool, and the public runbook in the customer portal.

If you're preparing a deployment, start by running the preflight bundle and open a deployment ticket with the manifest attached. For presales scoping use the Customer Requirements templates in the Customer Requirements Library section of this page and copy the answers into the gating questionnaire.
